hypotheses.justification: The other assumptions already imply this one. In any preorder with `[Add α] [Sub α] [OrderedSub α]`, addition is monotone. Suppose x ≤ y. The lemma `add_tsub_le_right` (line 68 of the same file, which needs only Preorder, Add, Sub and OrderedSub) gives x + c - c ≤ x ≤ y. Then `tsub_le_iff_right` turns this into x + c ≤ y + c. With commutativity from `AddCommSemigroup`, left monotonicity follows as well. So the theorem can be proved without `[AddLeftMono α]`, for example under `omit [AddLeftMono α] in`. Explicit proof: rewrite with `tsub_le_iff_left`, so the goal is a + c ≤ b + c + (a - b). Rewrite with `add_right_comm`, so the goal is a + c ≤ b + (a - b) + c. Close it with `tsub_le_iff_right.mp (add_tsub_le_right.trans le_add_tsub)`. Here `le_add_tsub : a ≤ b + (a - b)` (line 93) needs no monotonicity, and the chain `add_tsub_le_right.trans le_add_tsub` proves a + c - c ≤ b + (a - b). No degenerate cases are left out, because the argument is purely order-theoretic and holds for every preorder.
